outlook.statement: The Company remains confident in the long-term potential of India's capital markets and its ability to create enduring value through disciplined execution, continuous innovation, and sustained investment in technology and customer capabilities.
The Company is navigating an ongoing leadership transition, preserving values and culture while equipping the organisation to thrive in an increasingly digital financial ecosystem.

The market presented challenges in FY2025-26, yet our financial discipline allowed us to deliver a profitable year almost equal to previous year. This resilience stems from a clear corporate mandate i.e. focus on our core business and fortify our operational model. Our various spheres of business are on its way to achieve scale as we continue to invest in avenues which are beneficial for our growth. Our brand is now being recognised in India. Each of our business segments offer huge headroom for growth and we are well placed to benefit from this.

India's strong domestic fundamentals, policy continuity and structural advantages provide a foundation for sustained economic growth, though growth expectations for FY 2026-27 moderated to 6.6% amid global uncertainties and monsoon-related risks.
Rising retail participation and financial awareness across India, widening the addressable client base.
Leveraging Mutual Fund AUM growth, which surpassed Rs 700 Cr. in FY 2025-26.
Scaling fee-based lines such as wealth management, PMS, merchant banking and advisory to reduce dependence on transaction income.

Increasing adoption of digital platforms, data analytics and artificial intelligence is expected to further enhance efficiency, personalise investment experiences and support the next phase of growth across India's financial services landscape.

The Company has a well-defined risk management framework in place. The risk management framework works at various levels across the enterprise. The Board of Directors monitor, report and mitigate various risks faced. The outcome of this process is reported to the Audit Committee.
Economic slowdown or prolonged low-volatility market reducing investor participation and trading volumes
Regulatory changes across broking and insurance-distribution businesses
Market risk on proprietary trading and inventory positions from sharp movements in equity, commodity and currency markets
Competition from established full-service firms and digital-first discount brokers exerting downward pressure on pricing
Operational failures in processes, people or systems disrupting service, settlement and reporting
Client defaults or insufficient margin during trading exposing the Company to financial loss
Cyber-attack, system failure and data breach on digital platforms
Inaccurate or incomplete financial reporting compromising decision-making and regulatory standing
Capital and funding risk in managing working capital and growth requirements while managing cost and maturity of borrowings
Geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility compressing trading volumes and brokerage income
Rising delinquencies in unsecured personal and business loans impacting NBFC lending business
Measures to curb speculative derivative trading reducing industry-wide F&O volumes and related brokerage income
Evolving regulatory and compliance requirements raising operating cost and complexity
Cybersecurity and technology risk across client-facing digital channels
Inherent limitations of internal financial controls including possibility of collusion or improper management override
Projections of internal financial controls to future periods subject to risk of inadequacy due to changes in conditions or deterioration in compliance
